analysis:
Examined the release toolchain bump: docs/operations/provider-release.md, mise.toml, scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh, scripts/provider_release_resume/identity.py and scripts/test-provider-release-toolchain.py. I found no concrete security regression.

The script now has two modes, release and qualification. Release mode accepts only SDK 27.2 with Swift 6.4.2 or 6.4.2.x. Qualification mode accepts SDK 27.2 or 27.0 with Swift 6.4.x. The Swift version match is anchored, so 6.40 and 6.4.20 are rejected. SDK versions are normalized and parsed with failures treated as rejection. An unknown mode exits 2. When no toolchain is accepted the script exits 1 before writing GITHUB_ENV, and the tests cover this. It may now export DEVELOPER_DIR, chosen only from the image's Xcode or from Xcode*.app directories under /Applications, or under DARKBLOOM_XCODE_APPLICATIONS. This keeps Metal and signing on the same Xcode as the Swift build. An explicit DEVELOPER_DIR remains the sole candidate. The wrapper symlink now uses the script's own directory instead of GITHUB_WORKSPACE, which is neutral or slightly better. No secrets, network access or new trust-boundary crossings are added.

The change does not touch the provider runtime threat model (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, T-034, T-054). It affects only build-toolchain provenance for the signed artifact.

Open questions for integration, since the workflows are not in the supplied evidence:
(1) DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN defaults to qualification, which is the more permissive mode. If release-provider.yml or the signing jobs do not set it to release, release builds could accept SDK 27.0 and Swift 6.4. That would conflict with the docs and with the build_sdk_version=27.2 recorded at scripts/provider_release_resume/identity.py:82.
(2) identity.py:82 hardcodes build_sdk_version as 27.2 instead of deriving it from the retained artifact. A retained unsigned artifact built under 27.0 before this change and resumed afterward would be mislabelled unless downstream verification checks the artifact's real SDK. Downstream verification was not supplied.
